metadata.case_name: CHAN SIU YIM v. DR CHEUNG SHEUNG KIN ALSO KNOWN AS DR SAMUEL KINNETH CHEUNG

injuries.description: extraction of the lower left first pre-molar (“tooth 34”) from the plaintiff.
source: At the appointment that took place on 13 December 2007, without any prior notice to the plaintiff and without the plaintiff’s consent, the defendant extracted the lower left first pre-molar (“tooth 34”) from the plaintiff.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of teeth or supporting structures

injuries.description: Occlusion problem including increased overjet and shifted lower dental midline to the left (malocclusion / worsening inter-arch relationship).
source: A number of problems emerged after the commencement of the treatment, including occlusion problem which affected her chewing; upper teeth displaced and shifted to the left and overjet of the upper teeth increased.
after receiving the defendant’s treatment, the plaintiff had an overjet of 3.5mm while the overjet had been 1-2mm before the treatment commenced.
the centerline had been shifted to the left by 2mm, and when the plaintiff began to receive remedial treatment from Dr Tong, her midline of the lower jaw was off to the left by 4mm.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of teeth or supporting structures

injuries.description: Adjustment disorder (psychiatric condition) arising from the unsatisfactory dental treatment.
source: diagnosed with adjustment disorder with insomnia.
The plaintiff is suffering from adjustment disorder with anxiety and depressed mood, which is caused by the unsatisfactory dental treatment from 2007 to 2010.

manifestations.description: Difficulty chewing; unable to chew properly.
Upper teeth displaced and shifted to the left (dental displacement).

treatments_received: Application of brackets and wire by the defendant as part of orthodontic treatment.
After 30 sessions of treatment by Dr Tong, the whole remedial process was completed in August 2012.
Consultation with psychiatrist in the Prince of Wales Hospital; prescribed anti-depressant and benzodiazepine.
Expert opinion that tooth 34 "needed to be replaced with a dental implant during the remedial treatment phrase."
treatments_future: Continue receive psychological as well as psychiatric treatment for another 6 months after this case is settled (Joint Report) — private sector cost about HK$25,000; court allowed claim for public hospital cost HK$1,000.

losses.description: Loss of lower left first premolar (tooth 34).

losses.category: Loss of ability to enjoy food and drink

losses.description: Plaintiff and her boyfriend had arguments and eventually broke up; plaintiff remains single to date; the defendant's negligence was regarded as a factor contributing to the breaking up.

comparable_cases.case_name: Wong Yuen Mei v Young Yau Yau Cecilia
comparable_cases.injury_description: Dentist extracted 4 first pre-molars causing unfit occlusion, headache, depression, anxiety and insomnia, unable to chew properly, loss of weight and appetite and other problems; after remedial treatment decreased longevity of the teeth and increased risk of tooth decay.

comparable_cases.case_name: Mak Po Ling v Young Yau Yau Cecilia
comparable_cases.injury_description: Extraction of three teeth with resultant problems similar to Wong Yuen Mei; plaintiff was a flight attendant and condition significantly improved after treatment.
